non_claims: Ribose versus arabinose or xylose, the anomeric configuration and the sugar ring size are not resolved.
Ribose, 2'-deoxyribose and 2'-O-methylribose are told apart by the precursor composition hypothesis, not by these ions.
Positional isomers of methylated bases (for example m1A versus m6A, m3C versus m5C) are not resolved.

notes: measure:false, provisional (WS0 2026-11-19, pending the author): in the 5-methylcytosine entries (12 of 156 hypotheses) the fragment C4H5N2+ is [B+H]+ minus NH3 and CO, so base ion and fragment can be one channel.

competitors.note: Pseudouridine, a C-glycoside isomer of uridine, generally gives no protonated base ion and loses water and part of the sugar instead (Dudley 2005; Giessing 2011).

priors.note: Loss of ribose (132 Da) to the protonated base is the rule for N-glycosidic nucleosides; any other sugar loss points to a modified sugar.
Almost all stable modified 2'-deoxyribonucleosides lose 2'-deoxyribose (116 Da) to the base ion.
2'-O-methylated nucleosides lose 146 Da and give the unmodified base ion.

terms.note: Protonated base [B+H]+ after loss of the whole sugar (132, 116 or 146 Da) from [M+H]+.
Base fragment from HCN, NH2CN, HNCO, CH3CN, methylamine or ketene loss of [B+H]+; ion traps show it only at MS3.
NH3 or H2O loss from [B+H]+; a generic loss, reported only.
Protonated pentose ion C5H9O4+ (133); weak, mainly for less basic nucleosides such as uridine; no deoxy or 2'-O-methyl sugar ion is printed.
